title: Two Processions
subtitle: Two groups booked the same square for the same evening
coldOpen: Two processions booked Civic Square for the same evening.
One was approved by a clerk; the other by his supervisor.
Both groups are already decorating opposite ends.

briefing.grievance: A cultural association and a residents’ welfare group each hold a permit for the square tonight. Each says the other is trying to steal its evening. Neither will move.
knownFacts: Both permits are genuine and were issued on the same day by different officers.
The square holds about 3,000 people; each group expects 2,000.
A hospital route runs along the square’s north edge.
unverifiedClaims: A post says one group plans to “take the square by force” at dusk.
A message says the police have secretly cancelled the second permit.
briefing.responsibility: You run the square’s permits and the policing plan. Both groups have the same right to be there; the square does not have room for both at once.
briefing.objective: Find a lawful, equal arrangement before dusk, keep the hospital route clear, and defuse the force rumour.

rightsMoments.question: Two groups hold valid permits for the same square. What does equal treatment require?

options.text: The same reasonable conditions for both, and an arrangement that lets both exercise their right if space allows.
options.feedback: Correct. Equality means neither group is favoured; the office’s error is not a reason to cancel one side.

options.text: Cancel the later permit; the first applicant wins everything.
options.feedback: Where both can be accommodated, cancelling one side is not required and treats the office’s mistake as that group’s fault.

options.text: Cancel both so nobody can complain of favouritism.
options.feedback: Cancelling both restricts two lawful assemblies to avoid an administrative decision.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 14 (equality) and Article 19(1)(b) (peaceful assembly) together require even-handed conditions and the least restrictive arrangement that meets safety.
rightsMoments.why: The square had room for two stages; the only thing missing was an office willing to say it had double-booked.

simple.question: Two groups both have permits for the same square. What is fair?

options.a: The same rules for both, and room for both if it fits.
options.b: Cancel the later permit. First one wins everything.

feedback.a: Yes! Treat both the same and make room for both.
feedback.b: No. The office’s mistake is not the second group’s fault.
feedback.c: Cancelling both punishes everyone for an office error.

simple.principle: Everyone is treated the same. Both groups may gather if the space allows.
simple.why: The square had room for two stages. The office just had to admit it double-booked.
